stem: A transplant recipient who helps care for young grandchildren asks about diaper changes after a grandchild received a live-virus vaccine. Which teaching point aligns with standard infection-prevention references?

options.text: Avoid changing diapers of children who were recently vaccinated with live-virus vaccines
Live-vaccine shedding never occurs after pediatric vaccination
Diaper changes are unrestricted regardless of recent vaccinations
Only hospital staff may change diapers for vaccinated children

explanation.rationale_correct: Infection-prevention teaching includes avoiding changing diapers of children who were recently vaccinated, because shedding after live-virus vaccines may continue for days, weeks, or months.

rationale_incorrect.B: Shedding after live-virus vaccination may persist for a variable period depending on vaccine and host factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Recent live-vaccine exposure warrants precautions including avoiding diaper changes when possible.
rationale_incorrect.D: Household caregivers are taught these precautions rather than deferring all diaper care to hospital staff.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → vi. Others
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Avoid changing diapers of children who were recently vaccinated

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → vi. Others (avoid diaper changes for recently live-vaccinated children); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Live-vaccine diaper-precaution angle distinct from household live-vaccine contact combo (cctc-1048) and garden/dirt gloves teaching (cctc-1140); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: When teaching routine infection-prevention measures at home, which wound-care step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Clean and cover recent cuts or wounds
Leave all cuts uncovered to promote air drying
Ignore minor skin breaks because immunosuppression prevents infection
Apply only topical steroids to all wounds without cleaning

explanation.rationale_correct: Infection-prevention teaching for other exposures includes cleaning and covering recent cuts or wounds, along with completing prescribed infection prophylaxis or treatment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cleaning and covering recent wounds is recommended rather than leaving cuts uncovered.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppressed recipients remain at infection risk and require wound care.
rationale_incorrect.D: Wound cleaning and covering are standard rather than applying steroids without cleaning.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → vi. Others
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Clean and cover recent cuts or wounds

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

notes: Source-first item. Wound-cleaning precaution angle distinct from garden gloves/mask teaching (cctc-1140) and surgical wound infection management (cctc-3051); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A transplant recipient planning international travel asks how to choose a destination. Which counseling factor aligns with standard travel references?

options.text: Risk of infection, including risk of endemic infections in the area
Endemic infection risk should be ignored when selecting travel destinations
Only flight duration matters; local disease patterns are irrelevant
Recipients should select destinations based solely on leisure activities

explanation.rationale_correct: Travel destination selection considers current health and physical limitations and risk of infection, including endemic infections in the area.

rationale_incorrect.B: Endemic infection risk is specifically included in destination planning.
rationale_incorrect.C: Local infection and endemic disease patterns are part of destination selection rather than being irrelevant.
rationale_incorrect.D: Health and infection risk are weighed along with other travel factors rather than ignoring medical considerations.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → o. Travel → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Risk of infection, including risk of endemic infections in area

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → o. Travel → ii. (destination selection includes endemic infection risk); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Endemic-infection destination-risk angle distinct from early travel-away-from-home restriction (cctc-1134) and destination-provider planning (cctc-1136); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant travel-preparation teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Patients should consider travel insurance and purchase of a medic alert tag.
Patients should bring a basic first-aid kit that includes a thermometer.
Destination selection should ignore endemic infection risk.
Patients should bring a summary of health history including surgical procedure and current medications.

explanation.rationale_correct: Travel insurance and medic alert tags, a first-aid kit with thermometer, and a health-history summary are supported. Statement III is false because endemic infection risk is a destination-selection consideration.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—a health history and medication summary should be carried when traveling.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because infection and endemic disease risk should be considered when choosing destinations.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: travel insurance and purchase of a medic alert tag … first-aid kit that includes a thermometer … Risk of infection, including risk of endemic infections … Summary of health history including surgical procedure and current medications

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → o. Travel → ii., v., vi. (endemic risk, first-aid kit, medic alert/travel insurance, health summary); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Travel-preparation combo distinct from travel-restriction/carry-on combo (cctc-1137) and endemic-risk one-best (cctc-1144); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.
